A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Gradient Slingshots research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–D support comparison; v4 also includes a readable NeurIPS checklist.

before.justification: v3 reports original toy experiments, feature-visualization manipulation results across several architectures, a weapon-classification case study, and attack-detection experiments.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and adds ProxPulse comparisons, MACO evaluation, and analyses of additional and non-target neurons.

M1.justification: Equation (10) corrects the activation-based manipulation loss: the quadratic term changes sign and gains a factor of 1/2, while the constant changes sign. The tunnel construction, gradient-based loss, and preservation objective remain unchanged. This establishes a correction to the reported objective, not an implementation change or rerun.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same toy data, MNIST, CIFAR-10, TinyImageNet, ImageNet, ImageNet-Sketch targets, and weapon/penguin image collections. MACO and additional-neuron experiments vary visualization procedures and feature selection within the retained tasks and data coverage.

E2.justification: v3 discusses Prox-Pulse only as related work. v4 evaluates the same method, renamed ProxPulse, against GS on the ResNet-50 wolf-spider-to-Dalmatian setting at two ProxPulse trade-off settings. Appendix A, Table 4, and Figure 9 introduce the paper's first direct empirical comparison with another manipulation attack.

E3.justification: v4 adds CLIP target-label and ground-truth-label alignment metrics, expands alpha sweeps, and introduces MACO and neuron-control evaluation protocols. It also changes the reported Pixel-AM recipe from no gradient clipping to clipping and revises the CLIP case-study alpha from 0.99991 to 0.999915. These stated setting changes do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Appendices D.1–D.4 examine visualization stability, transfer of an already manipulated ViT-L/32 to MACO, effects on non-target ResNet-50 neurons, and manipulation of its first ten output neurons. These substantially extend robustness and feature-selection analyses. The earlier trade-off, target-image, and detection analyses are retained, with expanded trade-off evaluations.

E5.justification: Both versions' Appendix C.8 reports 100 FV samples per model except 30 for CLIP ViT-L/14. v4 explicitly explains that standard deviations describe variability across independently generated FVs, but its new Table 3 caption claims 100 case-study runs, contradicting the retained 30-run statement. Reporting changes are evident; an actual increase in runs is unresolved.

E6.justification: v4 adds baseline, MACO, non-target-neuron, additional-neuron, semantic-alignment, and expanded alpha-sweep results. Table 4 reports 75.13% accuracy for GS versus 69.03% and 58.51% for ProxPulse, with AUROC 1.00 for all three. Existing values also change: Table 3 reports 98.04% rather than 98.18% accuracy on other weapons, alongside a revised case-study alpha, so this is not an established same-setting deterioration.

T1.justification: Equation (2) moves regularization to the input of the feature function, and Equation (4) corrects the quadratic potential's sign to agree with the target-directed gradient. v4 also explicitly states gamma positivity and includes the initialization condition in Lemma 3.1. The convergence argument and overall theoretical construction are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion retain the same central contributions: manipulating FV toward arbitrary targets without architectural changes or substantial performance loss, and detecting manipulation through natural-domain activation maximization. The new experiments support these retained claims rather than redefining them.

C2.justification: v4 explains MACO's tiled outputs through its cropping recipe and adds interpretations concerning non-target preservation and avoidance of neuron cherry-picking. Section 7 specifies labeled test-data access for detection and characterizes MACO evidence as preliminary. The main memorization explanations and broader limitations remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: v4 supplies exact CLIP label prompts in Table 6, expands the hyperparameter-selection explanation with coarse-to-fine alpha search and weight/gradient heuristics, and identifies Horama for MACO evaluation. Most implementation, hardware, and code-access information is retained. Appendix C.10 removes the earlier two-hour case-study computation estimate.

R1.justification: v4 adds references to Baehrens et al., Samek et al., Kauffmann et al., Lucent, and Horama. It also extends the existing ProxPulse discussion with an empirical superiority claim. The broader positioning against architectural manipulation attacks remains unchanged; Prox-Pulse and ProxPulse are the same cited method.

P1.justification: v4 copyedits terminology and prose, expands the evaluation introduction, adds a Manipulation Results subsection, swaps the experimental-settings and metrics subsections, and appends a NeurIPS checklist. Affiliations and acknowledgements also change. The main narrative and organization remain recognizable.

P2.justification: v4 adds comparison and control figures/tables, a label-prompt table, and visualization galleries. Trade-off tables gain grouped alignment/similarity columns, with ResNet-50 MSE/SSIM details retained in a new appendix table. Existing displays are resized and relocated, and appendix figures are interleaved with corresponding tables. New Table 16 reverses the accuracy and AUC headers relative to their values.

improvement.justification: Corrected equations improve mathematical consistency, while the new ProxPulse comparison, MACO test, and neuron controls strengthen empirical support. These benefits are tempered by the conflicting case-study run counts, reversed headers in Table 16, and an overly broad non-target-preservation interpretation despite the hammerhead similarity change in Table 15. The net improvement is supported but qualified.
